_about: NIFTY analytics build -- the recipe the pipeline runs on.
python build_charts.py                                   builds with this file
Every key is optional: whatever is left out keeps the default in nifty/defaults.py.
A key whose name starts with '_' is a note and is ignored, so this file can explain
itself the way the TOML twin does with comments (a note named after a real setting,
such as '_enabled', is refused rather than ignored, so a note cannot switch one off).
An unknown section or key is refused rather than ignored, so a typo cannot quietly
change a build. Relative paths are relative to the project root.

instrument._note: what the sheet calls the tape it is showing
instrument.name: NIFTY 50

_note: what a build reads and where it writes; each index owns one output tree, so output/nifty holds this recipe's exports and sheet and output/sensex holds SENSEX's. The two never share a day folder (2026-10-16 exists in both).

sources_glob names the sessions; a dashboard (same name, _DASHBOARD.json) with no tape beside it is a session too, read from its own nifty_seconds series. When both files are there the tape wins: it runs to the last second of the closing minute.
The bar widths, in seconds: one chart tab and one CSV/JSON export each.
12s, 1m and 300 all parse; the list must not name the same width twice.

sma._note: The averages drawn on the price pane; they stay editable in the sheet's toolbar.

_note: The averages behind the analytics table and the CSV columns, and the percentage
precision every percentage is compared at. run_rule is the sentence the sheet
prints for the consecutive counts; it defaults in nifty/defaults.py.
The direction row: consecutive candles where the fast average sits above the slow
one while the slow one rises (ABOVE), or below it while the slow one falls (BELOW).
Both periods must appear in [analytics] periods above -- the row reads that
average's printed percentage change. The rule sentence is written from the two
periods unless it is overridden here.
The crossing row and the distance row beneath it.
cross direction : ABOVE when SMA {fast} was below SMA {slow} on the previous
candle and is above it on this one; BELOW for the mirror image;
empty on every other candle, and on an equal pair, which is
never a strict crossing.
distance (%)    : ((SMA {distance_from} - SMA {distance_to}) / SMA {distance_to})
* 100, read on the crossing candle only, at pct_decimals.
All four periods must appear in [analytics] periods above. The two rule sentences
are written from these periods unless they are overridden here.
The above/below relationship row: which side of each other two averages sit on,
one word per candle (ABOVE / BELOW), empty where they are equal or not available.
This is the CURRENT relationship, not a crossing: no previous candle is read. Both
periods must appear in [analytics] periods above. The rule sentence is written from
the two periods unless it is overridden here.
The green arrow: ONE rule, seven conditions, all of them required (AND). Four are
read from the candle itself, three from the candle before it. Every one of them is
an ordinary column the rows above already carry, so the rule invents no series of
its own and cannot disagree with what the table shows.
1. the crossing row reads cross_direction            (current candle)
2. the distance (%) at that cross is inside the window, both ends included
3. the above/below relationship reads relation       (current candle)
4. the session's dashboard, on the minute this candle opens in, reads
pe_oi_change above ce_oi_change                     (current candle)
5. the slow average's change (%) is strictly above chg_pct_min (previous candle)
6. the fast average's FALLING run is streak_minus_min..streak_minus_max,
while its rising run is 0                              (previous candle)
7. the slow average's RISING run is streak_plus_min or more (previous candle)
Each use_* boolean switches one condition on or off: true checks it, false skips
it. They are spelled out here rather than left to the built-in default, so this
file states the whole rule. use_flow off drops condition 4 only.
The red arrow is configured independently in red_signal below (the same seven
conditions read the other way round); [signal] red_arrow only applies when no
red_signal section is present and the red rule is the green rule's mirror.
The red arrow: ONE rule, seven conditions, all of them required (AND), for
SELL/SHORT signals -- the green rule's seven conditions read the other way round.
Four are read from the candle itself, three from the candle before it. Every one of
them is an ordinary column the rows above already carry, so the rule invents no
series of its own and cannot disagree with what the table shows.
1. the crossing row reads cross_direction            (current candle)
2. the distance (%) at that cross is inside the window, both ends included
3. the above/below relationship reads relation       (current candle)
4. the session's dashboard, on the minute this candle opens in, reads
ce_oi_change above pe_oi_change                     (current candle)
5. the slow average's change (%) is strictly below chg_pct_min (previous candle)
6. the fast average's FALLING run is streak_minus_min..streak_minus_max,
while its rising run is 0                              (previous candle)
7. the slow average's RISING run is streak_plus_min or more (previous candle)
Each use_* boolean switches one condition on or off: true checks it, false skips
it. use_flow off drops condition 4 only; a session with no dashboard never reads it.
An unknown key is refused rather than ignored, so a typo cannot quietly change a build.
Relative paths are relative to the project root.
The trade clock the backtest reads, in IST wall clock.
last_entry: no arrow whose candle opens after this is taken; a signal at the time
itself is still taken, and one after it is reported but not traded.
hard_exit: a position still open when the clock reaches this is closed there, at
that candle's opening price, whatever its profit or loss -- no trade is carried
past the hard exit.
The delivered sheet: its file name, its page title, and how many candles a chart
opens on. window_bars is a view, not a truncation -- the arrows, the table and both
exports always cover every candle. A double-click snaps a chart back to it.
